evidence: Small, flat package structure (3 top-level packages: http_prompt, tests, docs) with no service boundaries
High intra-package coupling visible in cross-module imports (e.g., execution.py imports from context, output, utils; completer.py imports from completion)
Shared context object (http_prompt.context.Context) used across modules (cli, execution, completer, etc.)
All functionality resides in a single deployable unit (one Python package 'http_prompt') with no external process communication
Clear vertical modularity by concern (cli, execution, context, completion, lexer, tree, etc.) rather than technical layers
Testing follows standard Python unittest/pytest conventions with test modules mirroring source modules
No explicit ports/adapters or ingress/egress mechanisms (e.g., no abstract interfaces for HTTP clients, filesystems, etc.)
risks: Potential for tight coupling as modules evolve without strict boundaries
Limited scalability for distributed features without refactoring
Difficult to adopt independent release cycles for components
